llm.summary: The skill advertises a narrow mobile-listing check but ships a broad authenticated ARI account CLI that can incur charges and change persistent ARI settings.

dimensions.detail: Authenticated network access to https://ari.funewa.com is expected, but the single bearer token can reach account-management and paid endpoints beyond the stated mobile-listing diagnostic purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: There is no dependency install or hidden installer, and the CLI uses the Python standard library; setup/configure can save an ARI API key to ~/.ari/config.json with 0600 permissions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions tell the agent to use only operations capabilities/profile/quote/run/status and collect when needed, but the bundled Bash-accessible CLI does not enforce that narrow allowlist.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No OS persistence was found, but the CLI can create or change persistent remote account state such as autoconfirm policy, collection schedules, competitors, watches, alert read state, and workbench statuses.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the reference docs limit the skill to the fixed listing/mobile workflow, but scripts/ari.py exposes many additional commands for analysis, recurring collection, competitors, watches, alerts, leaderboard, workbench status, advice, reports, and exports.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable granting the agent an ARI API key that can access broader ARI account features than mobile-listing diagnosis. Avoid enabling autoconfirm, do not use export --out on sensitive paths, and prefer a package version that technically restricts the CLI to the documented listing/mobile workflow.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Confirmed in substance: the artifact documents a narrow mobile Listing optimizer, while the inspected CLI is a general ARI review/product operations client.
[AE1] unexpected: Downgraded as a scanner coverage issue: scripts/ari.py was present locally and inspected; no analysis-evasion behavior was needed to explain the risk.
[LP1] unexpected: Partly confirmed: official-domain authenticated ARI access is disclosed, but broad account mutation and paid workflows are not proportionate to the narrow advertised workflow.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed: scheduling, watches, workbench actions, exports, leaderboard, and generic analysis materially expand the skill's authority beyond listing/mobile diagnosis.
[EA2] unexpected: Confirmed as a review concern: autoconfirm can be read and changed account-wide, and some paid analysis paths can rely on auto-confirmation rather than a fresh local confirmation.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-language docs and /zh links are visible throughout the package and do not by themselves create a security concern.
[T05] unexpected: Confirmed: the bundled CLI exposes remote mutations and paid account operations outside the declared skill scope.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed but limited: export --out can overwrite any path writable by the process; export is also outside the advertised narrow workflow.
